Title: Welcome to your first 90 days
What to do: Isa will guide you through your first 90 days as chapter president, a few steps at a time.

Title: Get to know Isa
What to do: Take a five-minute tour: what Isa can help with, how she shows her sources, and how to reach a person.

Title: Meet your Chapter Experience contact
What to do: Your contact is the person to reach when Isa can't help, or when you'd rather talk to someone. Book a welcome call, send an introduction, or join a group welcome.

Title: Read what your predecessor left you
What to do: Open your chapter's succession notebook to find the decisions, contacts and open items the previous president saved for you.

Title: Meet your board
What to do: See who else is on your chapter board, with their roles and time zones.

Title: Review your mission, vision and chapter history
What to do: Read your chapter's mission and vision statements and its organizational history.

Title: Introduce yourself to your board
What to do: Isa helps you write a short introduction email to your board, in your own words. It links to an optional four-question profile form, so board members can share what they're good at and how they'd like to help. You read, edit and send it yourself.

Title: Log in to ISACA's chapter systems
What to do: Sign in to the Chapter Leader Portal, your chapter's Engage site and Chapter 360, so you know where each one is. If you can't see your chapter leader tools yet, ISACA may not have your new role on record. Your Chapter Experience contact can help!
Source: ISACA Chapter Systems Overview; ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 8

Title: Check your chapter's leader listing
What to do: Look at the About Us page on your chapter's Engage site and make sure the board and leaders shown are correct and current.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 10 (Chapter Leader Listing on Hosted Chapter Websites)

Title: Meet Chapter 360
What to do: Take a short tour of Chapter 360, ISACA's resource for running your chapter: its six focus areas, its practice areas, and the yearly self-assessment.

Title: Check that volunteers have signed their agreements
What to do: Make sure every volunteer has signed the Conflict of Interest Statement and the Willingness to Serve Agreement and submitted them to the chapter's secretary.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 14 (President's Annual Checklist)

Title: Confirm the volunteer list reached ISACA
What to do: The list of volunteers appointed and elected at the AGM goes to the Chapter Experience team through ISACA Support. The outgoing president usually sends it. Confirm it has been sent.

Title: Hold your handoff meeting with the outgoing president
What to do: Meet the outgoing president to go over open items, records, contacts and ongoing activities that need your follow-up.

Title: Update the bank signers
What to do: Work with your Treasurer so the chapter's bank and financial accounts list the new authorized signers. Keep at least two signers; three is best.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 12 (Turnover Procedures); ISACA Annual Chapter Compliance Framework

Title: See your board's profile replies
What to do: See the profile replies your board members have sent so far. The form is optional, so some members may not reply, and you can finish this step whenever you're ready.

Title: Review committees and how meetings are run
What to do: Read your chapter's committee information and its meeting processes.

Title: Review your bylaws, policies and Chapter Affiliation Agreement
What to do: Read your chapter's bylaws and policies, and the Chapter Affiliation Agreement.

Title: Set your board meeting rhythm
What to do: Your board meets at least four times a year. Work with your Secretary to set the dates, times and format of this year's meetings and share them with the board.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 7 (Chapter Board Meetings); ISACA Annual Chapter Compliance Framework

Title: Day 30 check-in
What to do: Isa asks one question: what's still unclear? You choose whether to share your answer with your Chapter Experience contact.

Title: Review your strategic plan and financial summaries
What to do: Read your chapter's strategic plan and its financial summaries.

Title: Put all chapter events on your Engage site
What to do: Make sure all chapter events are listed on the chapter's Engage website.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 13 (President's Annual Checklist)

Title: Hold a strategic planning session
What to do: Develop the chapter's goals and strategies for the new year in a strategic planning session.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 14 (President's Annual Checklist)

Title: Plan an orientation for incoming chapter leaders
What to do: Plan an orientation for all incoming chapter leaders, covering mission and vision, history, bylaws and policies, strategic plan, financial summaries, committees, meeting processes and the Chapter Affiliation Agreement.
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 13 (President's Annual Checklist)

Title: Make sure your goals and strategic plan are in progress
What to do: The guidebook asks for the chapter's goals and strategic plans to be in progress within 60 days of the AGM. (The prototype counts from the term start date.)
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), p. 14 (President's Annual Checklist)

Title: Learn the compliance requirements
What to do: See what ISACA checks each year, which evidence is required, and when to submit: the annual review runs from 1 November to 31 December.

Title: Day 60 check-in
What to do: Isa asks one question: what's still unclear? You choose whether to share your answer with your Chapter Experience contact.

Title: Look at the year ahead
What to do: Go over the next dates on the President's Annual Checklist, including the compliance window and when to start recruiting next year's volunteers (within about 7 months of the AGM).
Source: ISACA President Guidebook (August 2026), pp. 13-14 (President's Annual Checklist)

Title: Day 90 check-in
What to do: Isa asks one question: what's still unclear? You choose whether to share your answer with your Chapter Experience contact.
